gaps.sentence: So convincing ___ her argument that even the sceptics agreed.
gaps.explanation: 'So convincing was her argument that …' — 'so + adj' fronted with inversion.

gaps.sentence: So convincing ___ his argument that nobody objected.
gaps.explanation: So + adjective at the front: was his argument that…

gaps.sentence: ___ it not been for your help, we would have failed.
gaps.explanation: Had it not been for = if it hadn't been for — fixed inverted conditional.

gaps.sentence: Hardly had we left the house ___ it started to pour.
gaps.explanation: Hardly … when — fixed pair; 'than' belongs to 'no sooner'.

gaps.sentence: Under no circumstances ___ the door be left unlocked.
gaps.explanation: 'Under no circumstances should/must the door be left unlocked' — modal + inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the play cancelled, but the theatre was closed as well.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only was the play cancelled' — inverted passive.

gaps.sentence: Only when the audit was complete ___ the accounts released.
gaps.explanation: Only when X happened were the accounts released — inversion after only when.

gaps.sentence: Never before that afternoon ___ so many goals been scored in one match.
gaps.explanation: 'Never before that afternoon' fixes the reference in the past: had so many goals been scored.
